title: False-positive / false-negative baseline

method.classification_rule: A case is adversarial or benign according to the fixture design described in ROADMAP.md; 'flagged' means the validator emitted at least one warning for that record id.
method.intent_source: ROADMAP.md v0.2 lists the adversarial fixture as covering false sources, inference/observation confusion, unsupported confidence, and stale evidence; the two remaining records act as controls.

cases.note: A plausible but false source is structurally well-formed. The validator does not and cannot assess source truth, so this case passes silently.
The observation/inference detector matches only the literal token 'interpretation:' inside an observation string. An inference written as plain declarative prose is not detected.

This is the fixture's intended good example, yet it warns. The warning fires on any high-confidence claim whose independence is not 'independent', so a verified primary source and an unverified single source are treated identically.

findings.finding: The validator cannot detect a convincing false source.
findings.implication: Structural validation must not be read as truth validation. This is already stated in PROJECT.md; the baseline makes it measured rather than asserted.

findings.finding: Inference written as declarative prose passes as an observation.
findings.evidence: inference-labelled-as-observation is unflagged because the detector requires the literal token 'interpretation:'.
findings.implication: Rule 1 of the README is enforced only for one surface form.

findings.finding: The high-confidence warning does not distinguish a verified primary source from an unverified single source.
findings.evidence: verified-primary-source warns while being the fixture's intended good example.
findings.implication: The most valuable warning is also the noisiest, which weakens its use as a decision gate.

findings.finding: Every fixture exits 0 whether or not warnings are emitted.
findings.evidence: Both fixtures returned exit_code 0 with different warning counts.
findings.implication: Validation is warning-only. As-is it cannot gate a merge; the roadmap's 'warning-only vs decision gate' experiment has a concrete starting number.

known_limits: Intent labels come from fixture design and roadmap text, not from an independent external oracle.
Two runs are enough to show determinism, not to estimate variance.
Classification is per record id; the validator has no per-case assertion mechanism, so this baseline is external to it.
